messages:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: Alert firing — hosted-prod / generation-stream — p99 latency > 3.5s for 5m. Alert: /alerts/hosted-prod-generation-stream/p99-high

maya (SRE, oncall): oncall here, investigating. paging ryan.

ryan (SRE): I'm on it, joining. grabbing grafana and s3 traces now.

maya (SRE, oncall): quick status — customer reports streaming stalls and partial responses. p95 also elevated.

dani (eng-runtime): saw a push 25m ago to streaming-optimizations canary. any rollout?

ops-bot: Deploy bot: rollout/streaming-optimizations canary -> 30% traffic at 2026-03-14T02:38:00Z.

ryan (SRE): confirmed. dashboards: p95 went from ~600ms -> 1.8s; p99 jumped to 4.6s. error rate not increased, so it's latency-only.

maya (SRE, oncall): first triage checklist: 1) Are autoscaler metrics healthy? 2) Any kernel errors in runtime? 3) Is fallback path functional?

ryan (SRE): running quick checks —
```
kubectl -n hosted-prod get hpa streaming-workers
kubectl -n hosted-prod logs deploy/streaming-runtime -c runtime | tail -n 200
```

ryan (SRE): HPA shows desired=8 current=4; scale target CPU 70% but pods at ~65%. autoscaler didn't ramp because CPU threshold not breached. shows backlog queue growing.

dani (eng-runtime): runtime logs show repeated "kv_cache MISS, fetching prefix" and `grpc: stream stalled, no frames for 12s` entries. looks like KV cache eviction/latency regression after the canary.

jules (product): customers with streaming heavy usage (Customer X, Customer Y) reported timeouts. ticket inbound from Customer X saying UI shows spinner > 30s.

maya (SRE, oncall): impact: partial streaming stalls causing client timeouts for some sessions. SLOs degraded for hosted-api route. likely Sev2.

ryan (SRE): immediate mitigation options: 1) rollback canary -> safe but slow; 2) enable fallback to smaller model (gpt-lite-ptq) for streaming routes; 3) force scale streaming-workers to 12; 4) short-term route a % of traffic to dedicated pool. thoughts?

dani (eng-runtime): canary touches kernel selection path and KV cache config. fast rollback is doable (kubectl rollout undo), but may take ~3-5 mins to stabilize. enabling fallback routing is faster via feature flag.

maya (SRE, oncall): do fallback first + force scale. try rollback if that doesn't bring p99 down in 10 mins.

ryan (SRE): executing now — enabling feature flag `streaming_fallback=gpt-lite-ptq` for hosted-prod (edge config) and `kubectl scale deployment/streaming-runtime --replicas=12`.

ops-bot: Feature flag updated: streaming_fallback -> gpt-lite-ptq (uid: ff_1223).

ops-bot: kubectl command accepted, scaling streaming-runtime -> 12 replicas.

ryan (SRE): tailing logs after actions. initial signs: dropped per-pod queue depth, some sessions reconnected. p95 trending down to ~900ms.

dani (eng-runtime): KV cache miss rate still elevated — need to warm prefix cache. triggering cache prefetch for top 20 prefixes. running script: `scripts/prefetch-prefixes --top 20 --env hosted-prod`.

maya (SRE, oncall): good. notify customers: jules can you prepare a short message for Customer X/Y? include ETA ~15-30m.

jules (product): will draft and send via CS. message: "We're investigating streaming latency issues affecting partial responses; mitigation in progress and we're routing some traffic to fallback models. More updates in 15m."

ryan (SRE): alert note: p99 fell to 2.1s after scaling + fallback. still above SLO but improving. keeping monitoring on.

dani (eng-runtime): I see request traces: canary variant increases cold KV reads due to changed sharding; the patch reduced prefix cache effectiveness. that matches stalls. recommend reverting canary.

maya (SRE, oncall): agreed — plan: continue fallback + scaled replicas -> if p99 < 1.2s in next 10m, hold; else rollback canary. also create incident ticket and page stakeholders.

ryan (SRE): creating incident on incidents.redwood.ai -> INC-2026-087. short summary included. paging oncall lead.

ops-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-087, severity=2. Incident channel: #incident-INC-2026-087.

jules (product): product impact note: sessions that need streaming token-by-token are affected; non-streaming batch customers less impacted.

maya (SRE, oncall): after 12m: p95 ~720ms, p99 ~1.5s. still borderline. do we want to rollback anyway?

dani (eng-runtime): I can roll back canary now. rollback will restore previous kernel/cache behavior. recommend rollback to be safe.

ryan (SRE): proceeding with rollback. `kubectl -n hosted-prod rollout undo deploy/streaming-optimizations --to-revision=1`

ops-bot: Rollout undo triggered.

ryan (SRE): rollback in progress. monitoring logs for any surge/errors.

maya (SRE, oncall): customer comms updated. CS posted interim message.

(6m later)

ryan (SRE): rollback completed. p95 ~480ms, p99 ~820ms. KV cache miss rate back to baseline. streaming stalls cleared.

jules (product): CS notified customers that mitigation succeeded; advising to reopen if they still see issues.

maya (SRE, oncall): handoff: I'm about to step out at 03:20 UTC. ryan, handing off monitoring to tony. summary: p99 regression caused by canary kernel change affecting prefix caching; mitigations applied: fallback model, forced scale, cache prefetch, rollback. incident INC-2026-087.

ryan (SRE): noted, thanks maya. tony, taking over. brief summary pinned in #incident-INC-2026-087.

tony (SRE): I'm here, taking oncall. will watch dashboards for the next hour and follow up with postmortem actions.

maya (SRE, oncall): thx — logging final notes then off. :wave:

ops-bot: Oncall handoff recorded: maya -> tony at 03:20 UTC.

ryan (SRE): post-incident next steps: 1) postmortem (assigned to dani + ryan) 2) add automated cache warm-up to rollout job 3) fix HPA target to consider queue length not just CPU 4) add regression alert for p99 after deploys. tagging owners in INC-2026-087.

dani (eng-runtime): will own the cache warm-up and regression alert. creating PR for rollout changes.

jules (product): I'll coordinate customer outreach and include status on the public status page.

tony (SRE): monitoring looks stable. closing immediate incident actions, leaving incident open for postmortem tasks.

ops-bot: Incident INC-2026-087 updated: status=stabilized, severity=2, postmortem: pending.

ryan (SRE): thumbs up. thanks team — good quick mitigation and rollback.

maya (SRE, oncall): back to sleep. :zzz:

(End thread)
